newsitem.title: UK: Esso cuts runs at Norway Slagen refinery - traders.
newsitem.headline: Esso cuts runs at Norway Slagen refinery - traders.

text.p: Esso has cut crude throughput at its refinery in Slagen, Norway by some 15 percent in response to falling margins, trading sources said on Monday.
Production at the 100,000 barrels per day facility was cut to around 85,000 bpd on Friday, the source said. Slagen does not have the sophisticated upgrading plant found at modern European refineries.
"It's a problem with margins," the source said. "We're still making money but we have an excess of gas oil products so there is little point making more."
Sources at Ireland's Whitegate refinery confirmed they were also cutting output to around 42-43,000 bpd from normal capacity of 65,000 bpd.
Several major European refineries cut back output last week in response to falling prices for their products.
- Texaco and BP cut runs at their jointly-owned 400,000 bpd Nerefco complex in the Netherlands by around 12 percent.
- Shell cut 12-15 percent of the 350,000 bpd output of its Rotterdam refinery, which has a nameplate capacity of 374,000 bpd.
- Daewoo cut runs at its 60,000 bpd Universal refinery in Antwerp by 15 percent to 50,000 bpd.
- Portuguese state oil company Petrogal reduced runs by around 40,000 bpd at its 210,000 bpd Sines refinery.
